// Improved classifier:
// - Uses global_stream_dir to opportunistically classify matching-direction IPs as GS,
//   but only when the CS signal is weak (avoids overriding strong CS).
// - Promotes to CS only when stride is stable and confidence is high.
// - Keeps CPLX when there is history of variability or when confidence indicates it.
// - Falls back to NL otherwise to reduce pollution.
// - Maintains simple hysteresis by respecting old_class in marginal cases.
ipcp::ip_class_t ipcp::classify_ip(int64_t old_stride, int64_t new_stride, int confidence, ip_class_t old_class)
{
  // No stride information -> next-line fallback
  if (new_stride == 0)
    return NL;

  // If a global stream is detected and this IP moves in the same direction,
  // prefer GS when we don't already have a strong CS signal.
  if (global_stream_dir != 0) {
    if ((global_stream_dir > 0 && new_stride > 0) || (global_stream_dir < 0 && new_stride < 0)) {
      if (confidence < CS_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD || old_class == GS) {
        return GS;
      }
    }
  }

  // Stable stride -> constant stride candidate
  if (new_stride == old_stride) {
    if (confidence >= CS_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD)
      return CS;
    // keep CS if previously classified (hysteresis)
    if (old_class == CS)
      return CS;
    // otherwise be conservative
    return NL;
  }

  // Stride changed: prefer CPLX if there is some evidence or prior CPLX classification
  if (old_class == CPLX && confidence >= 1)
    return CPLX;
  if (confidence >= CPLX_CONFIDENCE_THRESHOLD)
    return CPLX;

  // Default fallback
  return NL;
}
